description: the null-schema lane stops refusing a submission that carries `inputs`: K12's clause (C11:2902, row 8 C11:4727) becomes unreachable and every value a client sends is admitted on a record that declares no schema. Killed live by T-NULL-OBJ and T-NULL-EMPTY, which are [GW RI]/[HTTP RI] until IR-8a-1 rewires slot 8 — so the kill is NOT evidence (§3.2: only an [HTTP] kill of the unbound path is). The integrator re-runs this battery after the merge, when the same killers run unbound.

`{}` is read as "nothing was submitted" and passes: the one body a hostile client can always produce becomes the one body that is never refused. K12 refuses a submission CARRYING `inputs`, and §3.8 already distinguishes omitted from null from `{}` (P-F88). Killed live by T-NULL-EMPTY.

the lowering source is read BEFORE the decision instead of after it (D-2, plan §2.5): the read count per submission is unchanged, but a submission the gate then refuses has already loaded the class-C template and the turn join. Killed live by T-HELD and T-NULL-OBJ (their store-operation lists gain a second `WidgetIntentRecord.findFirst`) and by T-READ-ONCE (the reader is called on the refusal).

description: slot 8's pass carries a fact slot 8 does not produce (`loweredTurn`, whose producer is slot 9). J-1's `mergeFacts` throws on it — a fact has exactly one producer slot — so the submission raises instead of returning a verdict. This is the mutant the producer map is FOR: without `mergeFacts` the gate could hand Gate 13 a turn nobody appended. Killed live by T-NULL-NULL (the pass path), and at [U] by G8a-G3.

row 8's "enforced by refusal, never truncation", at the null lane: the gate REPAIRS the submission — it drops whatever `inputs` carried and decides on the repaired value, so `{a:1}` and `{}` both pass. A gate that repairs is a gate that does not refuse. Killed live by T-NULL-OBJ and T-NULL-EMPTY.
